newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russian insurers unite to keep out foreigners.
newsitem.headline: Two Russian insurers unite to keep out foreigners.

text.p: Two Russian insurance companies, SAO RESO-Garantia and ZAO ASKO-Peterburg have exchanged shares to brace themselves for foreign expansion to the market, senior company officials said on Wednesday.
RESO-Garantia has purchased 20 percent of ASKO-Peterburg, while ASKO-Peterburg has bought less than 20 percent of RESO shares, ASKO chief executive Lev Paneyakh told a news conference.
Both companies said the alliance was not a merger and that they would continue to exist independently.
"We have united mainly to oppose future foreign expansion," he said. "We have to unite insurers. It was the main basis for the union."

ASKO-Peterburg, which will change its name to ASK-Peterburg next year, will profit from RESO's 25 branches all over Russia, while RESO will benefit from a wide network of ASKO agents, said RESO president Sergei Sarkisov.
According to its own estimates, ASKO covers not less than 20 percent of the St Petersburg and Leningrad region market but is very poorly represented in Moscow, Paneyakh said.
Both companies plan to expand on the personal insurance market.
"It will take foreign companies years to set up a network and to train agents," he said. "We must have an advantage of time to fight off foreign expansion."

Russian legislation prohibits foreign insurance companies from acquiring more than 49 percent of a Russian insurer. But Paneyakh said smaller foreign companies did not always obey the rule, while the regulation would not last for ever.
Russia's nascent insurance market, represented by about 3,000 heavily undercapitalised companies, opposes any foreign presence, which is now very small.
However, Paneyakh said ASKO was in talks with an unnamed foreign company about purchasing ASKO shares.
He said ASKO was in talks with other Russian companies for deals similar to that with RESO.
Many Russian insurance companies see personal insurance as having the biggest potential in the market.
Russia's second biggest insurer SAO Ingosstrakh said this week it would expand its personal insurance operations and seek alliances with other Russian firms.

RESO-Garantia was set up in 1991 by Iberia Seguros of Spain, one of Russia's biggest banks, AKB Avtobank, and Ingosstrakh. Now RESO's shareholders include Russia's biggest bank Sberegatelny Bank RF, private airline Transaero and monopoly arms exporter Rosvooruzheniye.
